desc:
For every index i of the integer array nums, let left[i] be the sum of all elements strictly before i and right[i] the sum of all elements strictly after i. An empty side has sum 0.

Return the array answer with answer[i] = |left[i] - right[i]|.

nums = [10, 4, 8, 3]
left  = [0, 10, 14, 22]
right = [15, 11, 3, 0]
answer = [15, 1, 11, 22]
hints: Computing left[i] and right[i] with two inner loops costs O(n) per index. Which parts of those sums are shared between neighbouring indices?
Going from index i to i + 1, the left sum gains nums[i]. The right sum of i + 1 is the right sum of i minus nums[i + 1].
Compute the total once. Keep a running left and get the right side as total - left - nums[i], so a single pass is enough.
editorial: Let total be the sum of the whole array and let left be the running sum of the elements before the current index. Everything that is neither on the left nor the element itself is on the right, so right = total - left - nums[i]. For each index append abs(left - right) and then add nums[i] to left.

One pass for the total and one pass for the answers gives O(n) time. Only the output array is extra memory, so the working space beyond it is O(1). Storing full prefix and suffix arrays would give the same time but needs two more arrays.
solution:
def leftRightDifference(nums):
    total = sum(nums)
    left = 0
    out = []
    for x in nums:
        right = total - left - x
        out.append(abs(left - right))
        left += x
    return out
